newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish legislators seal 1997 budget draft.
newsitem.headline: Polish legislators seal 1997 budget draft.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament gave a final go ahead on Friday to the 1997 national budget after rejecting proposals to boost spending on agriculture.

In a series of votes, the house rejected most of the Senate's amendments to the bill which would have raised subsidies to farm credit and provided more funds for the food market regulating agency by a total of 220 million zlotys.
The finance ministry had warned that approving these amendments could have increased the budget deficit beyond the planned 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
"This is an ambitious budget as far as revenue targets are concerned. But they should be achieved due to our economic growth," Finance Minister Marek Belka said after the votes.
The budget now needs to be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski, which is seen as a formality.

The bill, seen as the continuation of the three previous budgets of the ruling leftsit coalition, envisages cutting year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December 1997 from last year's 18.5 percent. @
It provides for keeping GDP growth rate at 5.5 percent and slightly increasing real-term spending for most underfinanced areas such as education, health care, justice system and defence.
